record.program_name: Salinas Local Housing Trust Fund (Fund 2603) and Multifamily Housing NOFA gap financing (FY 2025-26 round, Resolution 23358)
record.administering_agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division (City Council sits as the Salinas LHTF Board of Directors)
record.typical_award_size: The June 24, 2025 Multifamily Housing NOFA offered about $8 million of gap financing; five proposals requested $17,981,000 and four were conditionally committed on November 18, 2025 (Resolution 23358) for $8,460,220: Vista de la Terraza rehabilitation (CHISPA, 40 units) $960,000 (CDBG $400,000, HOME $560,000); Saint George Apartments (CHISPA, 36 senior units) $3,017,699 including $1,432,000 LHTF, $397,000 HOME, $543,699 PLHA and $645,000 PLHA for land; Casentini Street Family Apartments (HACM and Milestone Housing, 88 units plus daycare) $3,837,000 ($570,000 LHTF, $3,267,000 HOME); Republic Cafe (City-owned, Chinatown) $1,290,521 LHTF. The Local Housing Trust Fund was established May 2, 2023; HCD awarded $3,807,248 in January 2024 against a $4,526,562 local match, and the City applied again in September 2024 for $1.5 million with a General Fund match of about $1.5 million. HSA, PLHA and PIP funds supply at least $100,000 a year of ongoing trust fund revenue.
record.per_unit_cap: None published; awards sized to the gap shown in the applicant pro forma.
record.affordability_requirement: LHTF-funded units restricted to 60% AMI or below (extremely low, very low and low income) under the City's LHTF program design; federal HOME and CDBG layers carry their own rent and income limits; 55-year covenants used on City loans.
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. The October 20, 2026 HLUC update (file 26-494) reports only on the four FY 2025-26 awards (NEPA and covenants pending; Casentini expects its tax credit result in November 2026; a Republic Cafe development partner RFP is planned by the end of 2026) and announces no new Multifamily NOFA. The City keeps an open application for shovel-ready HOME projects; contact the CDD Housing Division, (831) 758-7334.
record.layering_notes: Largest city-controlled pool in Monterey County. Stacks City HOME, CDBG, LHTF, PLHA and HSA money into one commitment that is then paired with 9% or 4% tax credits (Casentini applied September 8, 2026; Saint George applies after the City commitment). The County's Monterey County Housing Trust Fund (county record) is a separate pool that has not lent inside Salinas; County PLHA is also separate from the City's own PLHA (Salinas is a direct PLHA entitlement, see City PLHA record). The County-owned 855 East Laurel Drive Eden Housing project (county record) is in Salinas and may seek City gap funds in a future round. Blocked: cityofsalinas.org and salinas.gov return 403 to scripts; all material was read from the Salinas Legistar web API and legistar2.granicus.com attachments (staff report of October 20, 2026, Legistar file 26-494, and the September 10, 2024 LHTF staff report, file 24-480).
record.cycle_notes: Multifamily Housing NOFA last released June 24, 2025 (about $8 million; $8,460,220 conditionally committed November 18, 2025 by Resolution 23358). No FY 2026-27 or later NOFA found in Salinas Legistar items through November 8, 2026. Rounds have been issued when HOME, LHTF, PLHA and HSA balances accumulate rather than on a fixed annual date.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The October 20, 2026 NOFA update staff report (https://legistar2.granicus.com/salinas/attachments/9fda4d45-c093-4b0f-9973-ec713941c035.docx) states no prevailing wage rule for City LHTF gap loans. The State LHTF Round 5 NOFA (https://hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/lhtf/2024-lhtf-nofa.pdf) says LHTF Program funds are subject to state prevailing wage law unless a Labor Code 1720(c) exception applies as determined by DIR, which restates 1720. Local loans and grants are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1), (b)(4) and (b)(5) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720), but 1720(c)(5)(E) exempts privately owned residential projects whose only public participation is below-market interest rate loans with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI (applied to an NPLH loan in DIR PW 2019-018, https://dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2020/2019-018.pdf), and 1720(c)(3) exempts de minimis subsidies (under $600,000 and under 2 percent of project cost). Federal wages attach by source: HOME at 12+ HOME-assisted units (24 CFR 92.354, https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354) and CDBG at 8+ units (24 CFR 570.603, https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/570.603), which several NOFA awards carry.

record.program_name: Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA), City of Salinas five-year plan (direct entitlement)
record.administering_agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division
record.typical_award_size: Standard Agreement with HCD (June 2021) for up to $6,041,082 over the first five years; Fund 2951 Financial Assistance - Multi Family Housing appropriation $3,322,776.95 as of November 2024. Fourth plan amendment (November 19, 2024) set years three to five at 41% to 55% affordable housing development, 14% ADU production in year three, 40% homeownership in years three to five and 5% administration, and allocated $390,000 to CHISPA for three ADUs (138 Carr Avenue, 615 and 617 Fremont Street, rented up to moderate income) and $645,000 to CHISPA for land at 98 Kip Drive for 36 senior units. Earlier uses: Parkside Manor (2021), Fairview (Salinas Inn) Homekey acquisition with HACM ($2,500,000 of PLHA and PIP in 2025, 45 PSH units), SHARE Center homeless services. In January 2026 Council approved a PLHA-funded Mortgage Down Payment Assistance Program (deferred loans up to 150% AMI).
record.per_unit_cap: None stated; ADU awards averaged $130,000 per unit.
record.affordability_requirement: PLHA rules: rental development for extremely low to moderate income, ADUs up to moderate income, homeownership up to 150% AMI; City covenants recorded on assisted properties.
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. Multifamily PLHA dollars are committed through the City's Multifamily NOFA (Saint George Apartments $543,699 plus $645,000 for land) and no new NOFA has been announced. The PLHA-funded First Time Homebuyer Mortgage Down Payment Assistance Program ($1.3 million, deferred loans up to $125,000 or 17% of price, 3% interest, 30-year term, about ten loans) was projected to launch in November 2026.
record.layering_notes: Salinas receives its own PLHA formula allocation and does not share in the County PLHA plan (county record), which covers the unincorporated area plus Carmel-by-the-Sea, Greenfield and Soledad. PLHA pays land and predevelopment costs that HOME cannot (Saint George land $645,000), so it is usually the first City dollar in before a HOME or LHTF commitment. PLHA was also used as the local operating match for the Fairview Homekey PSH site now owned by HACM. Read through the Salinas Legistar API (file 24-570, November 19, 2024) because the City website blocks scripts.
record.cycle_notes: PLHA plan amendments require a 10-day public notice and Council hearing. Developer access to PLHA for rental projects is through the City's periodic Multifamily NOFA (last released June 24, 2025). The January 27, 2026 down payment program (HCD approved guidelines February 10, 2026) is a homebuyer program, not a developer funding round.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. HCD 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf) contain no prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon or Labor Code 1720 provision; the HCD PLHA FAQ (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/cycle-2-nofa-faq.pdf) says only that HCD programs require compliance with applicable law including prevailing wages unless the project meets a Labor Code 1720(c) exception as determined by DIR. PLHA loans and grants are public funds under 1720(b)(1) and (b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720), but 1720(c)(5)(E) (below-market loans with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI), 1720(c)(5)(C) (mortgage, down payment or single-family rehab aid to a household) and 1720(c)(3) de minimis can apply. Davis-Bacon applies only if HOME (12+ HOME units, 24 CFR 92.354) or CDBG (8+ units, 24 CFR 570.603) is layered. The City PLHA loan agreement for 98 Kip Drive (Section 4.8, https://legistar2.granicus.com/salinas/attachments/5511d6de-a40f-4ae2-b0f5-84fb2457e145.pdf) only requires the borrower to indemnify the City for any failure to pay prevailing wages as determined under Labor Code 1720 et seq. or Davis-Bacon; it does not declare the project a public work. The November 19, 2024 staff report (https://legistar2.granicus.com/salinas/attachments/8a30f094-b850-4395-ab8d-10e7d7026de0.docx) is silent.
record.audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: true changed to unclear.

record.program_name: CDBG, HOME and ESG entitlements, FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan (PY 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan and Alisal Neighborhood Revitalization Strategy Area)
record.administering_agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division
record.typical_award_size: FY 2026-27 resources $3,308,936: CDBG $2,196,140 plus $37,000 program income; HOME $844,248 plus $40,000 program income; ESG $191,548. CDBG recommendations: administration $446,628, Habitat for Humanity housing rehabilitation $440,000, Alisal NRSA sidewalks and streetlights $460,000, Chinatown neighborhood improvements $220,000, playground equipment $366,512, ECHO housing rights $100,000, Salinas Outreach and Response Team $200,000. HOME: $669,185 reserved for a shovel-ready affordable housing project (agency to be determined), $126,638 CHDO set-aside, $88,425 administration. ESG: $177,182 rapid rehousing. HOME-ARP $2,918,774 (2023) funds supportive services at Fairview Homekey ($1,190,337 to HACM, February 2026). The City is also the HCD ESG Administrative Entity for the Monterey/San Benito CoC.
record.per_unit_cap: HOME subsidy limits per HUD; no local cap.
record.affordability_requirement: HOME and CDBG income limits (80% AMI and below) with HOME rent and period-of-affordability rules; City loans typically carry 55-year covenants.
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. The FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan was due to HUD by August 16, 2026. For FY 2026-27 the City self-directed CDBG and ESG instead of issuing its usual annual NOFA, and HOME ($669,185 plus a $126,638 CHDO set-aside) is reserved for shovel-ready affordable housing projects through an open application with no deadline. No FY 2027-28 NOFA notice found as of November 8, 2026.
record.layering_notes: Salinas is the only HOME participating jurisdiction in Monterey County besides the Urban County (county record covers unincorporated Monterey plus Gonzales, Greenfield, Marina and Sand City; Salinas is not in it). HOME and CDBG are usually committed through the City's multifamily NOFA (Vista de la Terraza $400,000 CDBG and $560,000 HOME; Casentini $3,267,000 HOME over several years) and require HUD NEPA clearance before covenants are signed. The Alisal NRSA designation (adopted June 17, 2025) relaxes CDBG public benefit rules in East Salinas. Section 108 loan guarantees are listed as a possible future tool. Read through the Salinas Legistar API (file 26-214) and the draft AAP PDF on legistar2.granicus.com.
record.cycle_notes: The City typically runs an annual CDBG, HOME and ESG NOFA through citydataservices.net with a deadline at least 30 days after notice, but skipped it for the FY 2026-27 plan and self-directed funds. HOME requests for shovel-ready projects are accepted at any time. Action Plan public comment runs in May, HLUC review in May, Council hearing in June, HUD submittal by mid August.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

record.program_name: Housing Successor Agency (former Salinas Redevelopment Agency) Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund loans
record.administering_agency: City of Salinas as Housing Successor Agency; Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division
record.typical_award_size: Gap loans from the HSA Affordable Housing fund awarded through the City's annual housing NOFA. Example: $500,000 at 0% for 55 years to Sun Rose Housing, LLC (Interim, Inc.) for the 11-unit Sun Rose Apartments at 439 Soledad Street (8-bed transitional unit plus 9 permanent supportive units), approved December 6, 2022 after an $800,000 construction cost gap; the same site earlier received an $80,000 RDA grant (2000) and $500,000 CDBG (2021). HSA funds are also pledged as part of the $100,000 a year ongoing revenue for the Salinas Local Housing Trust Fund.
record.affordability_requirement: Very low and low income (HSA law caps use at 80% AMI with at least 30% of expenditures for extremely low income over five-year periods); 55-year deed restrictions on assisted projects.
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. HSA gap loans are awarded through the City's periodic housing NOFA (the Sun Rose loan came from the February 2022 NOFA; the most recent Multifamily NOFA opened June 24, 2025) and no new NOFA was announced in Salinas Legistar items through November 8, 2026.
record.layering_notes: The former RDA housing set-aside is the most flexible local layer (no NEPA, 0% long-term loans) and has been used to close inflation gaps on projects that already hold CDBG or HOME. Combine with Monterey County Behavioral Health (MCHOME program) services funding for PSH, and with County HHAP for operating support (county records). Fund balance was not published in the documents opened; confirm with the Housing Division before underwriting. Read through the Salinas Legistar API (file 22-560, December 6, 2022 staff report) because the City website blocks scripts.
record.cycle_notes: HSA Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund money is offered through the City's housing NOFA alongside HOME, CDBG, LHTF and PLHA when balances allow, not on a fixed annual date. Fund balance is reported in the annual Housing Successor report filed with the Housing Element APR.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Labor Code 1720(c)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) provides that affordable units built or rehabilitated under Health and Safety Code 33334.2(a)(5) or (a)(7) and paid for solely from the Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund (or that fund plus private funds) are not paid for out of public funds; mixed with other public sources, LMIHAF loans fall under 1720(b), subject to 1720(c)(5)(E). The Sun Rose loan agreement and staff report (https://legistar2.granicus.com/salinas/attachments/0d41207c-ec60-4cda-9217-2638669ddda9.docx, https://legistar2.granicus.com/salinas/attachments/af183231-2b0f-4cec-a1a4-1658dd2e5789.docx) contain no prevailing wage term. Sun Rose also carried CDBG, which brings Davis-Bacon at 8 or more units under 24 CFR 570.603.

record.program_name: Prohousing Designation and Prohousing Incentive Program (PIP) awards, Fund 2958
record.administering_agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division
record.typical_award_size: Salinas holds an HCD Prohousing Designation (application authorized November 29, 2022). PIP Round 1 award $1,650,000 funded an Affordable Housing Program and a First Time Homebuyer Down Payment Assistance Program; Rounds 2 and 3 applications (2024) were not funded; the Round 4 application for $1,250,000 (authorized March 24, 2026, proposing $1,000,000 for the City-owned El Rey Motel and $250,000 for down payment assistance) was also not funded: HCD's Round 4 awardee list ($11,299,410.78 total) shows Salinas (PDP score 58) unfunded and deprioritized because it received a prior-round award. PIP funds were also matched with PLHA ($2,500,000 combined) for HACM's Fairview Homekey acquisition in 2025. Round 5 offers about $8 million statewide.
record.affordability_requirement: PIP allows rapid rehousing, rental assistance, shelters, new construction, rehabilitation and preservation of permanent and transitional housing, and homeownership assistance up to 150% AMI.
record.next_deadline: PIP Round 5 applications due March 31, 2027 (NOFA released October 13, 2026; awards expected June 2027). Jurisdictions funded in earlier rounds, including Salinas, are funded only after all previously unfunded eligible applicants receive awards.
record.layering_notes: The designation is a scoring layer for developers applying to state programs for Salinas sites, and PIP money has been redeployed locally to PSH acquisitions and down payment assistance. Pairs with the City-County MOU to pursue Encampment Resolution Funds Round 5 for the El Rey Motel. No other Monterey County priority city held the designation in the documents opened; Marina submitted a draft application in August 2025 and Soledad states it is pursuing one. Read through the Salinas Legistar API (file 26-111, March 24, 2026 staff report).
record.cycle_notes: HCD PIP runs roughly annual rounds. Round 4 NOFA September 30, 2025, applications due March 31, 2026, Salinas not funded. Round 5 NOFA October 13, 2026, applications due March 31, 2027, Prohousing Designation required by March 31, 2027, awards June 2027.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The HCD Prohousing Incentive Program guidelines (2026) and Round 4 NOFA (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/pip-final-guidelines-2026.pdf, https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/pip-round-4-nofa.pdf) contain no prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon or Labor Code 1720 provision, and the City Round 4 staff report (https://legistar2.granicus.com/salinas/attachments/eb51f7bb-7071-4436-a9a1-b3d4b24621b8.docx) is silent. PIP-funded down payment assistance is exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C); PIP-funded rehab of City-owned property such as the El Rey Motel would be public works under 1720(a)(1) if construction is paid with those funds.

record.program_name: Density bonus (Zoning Code Section 37-50.060) and Zoning Code Update Phase 1 housing law amendments (2026)
record.administering_agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Planning Division
record.typical_award_size: Requirement and incentive, not a subsidy. Section 37-50.060 implements Government Code 65915 to 65917 with density bonuses, concessions (listed in subsection (k)) and parking reductions for very low, lower and moderate income, senior, day care and land donation projects, and adds a City density bonus for affordable senior housing (a 2014 senior project received a 100% bonus and 29% parking reduction). The Phase 1 Zoning Code Update ordinance (Planning Commission July 15, 2026; Council adoption August 2026, file 26-378) amended the density bonus, employee housing, two-unit development, ADU and emergency shelter provisions to match current state law and Housing Element Programs 4, 6, 7 and 14, and removed covered parking requirements for some residential uses. Phase 2 (objective design standards, General Plan consistency) is due mid-2027 and Phase 3 (new code) by end of 2027.
record.affordability_requirement: State density bonus law thresholds (5% very low, 10% lower, 10% moderate for-sale, 100% affordable), 55-year rental covenants; affordable rent defined at 30% of 50% AMI (very low) and 30% of 60% AMI (lower).
record.next_deadline: Not applicable; by-right with the planning application. Watch the Vision Salinas 2040 General Plan draft (summer 2026) and Phase 2 zoning amendments (mid-2027) for new objective standards and West Area and Central Area Specific Plan sites (five tentative maps totaling 3,206 units in process in 2025).
record.layering_notes: No local trust fund money attaches to the bonus; it is the entitlement layer that is combined with the City's LHTF, HOME, PLHA and HSA loans. Bonus units are excluded when computing inclusionary obligations, and the Downtown inclusionary exemption plus the 2026 SB 423 streamlining (467 and 479 East Market Street hearing September 2025) make Chinatown and downtown the easiest sites. Code text read on the zoneomics mirror because municode and the City site block scripts; the Phase 1 ordinance staff report was read through the Salinas Legistar API.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

record.program_name: CDBG entitlement and PLHA, two-year Notice of Funding Availability FY 2026-27 and FY 2027-28
record.administering_agency: City of Monterey Community Development Department, Housing Programs (Colton Hall, 570 Pacific Street, (831) 646-3995)
record.typical_award_size: CDBG entitlement about $250,000 a year ($242,234 in FY 2026-27) plus unusually large program income (estimated $1,023,166 in FY 2026-27; $493,697 from Hotel Pacific loan repayments and English Avenue rents and $729,609 from resale of inclusionary units in 2025), total CDBG resources $1,265,400. FY 2026-27 uses: Affordable Housing Opportunities $940,000 (inclusionary unit acquisition, rehabilitation and resale, minor and major homeowner rehabilitation loans), public services $207,400 (eleven nonprofits including shelters at about $20,000 each), administration $118,000; backup projects include a MidPen project ($1,500,000). PLHA (about $180,952 in 2025) goes to homeless services (PLHA Activity 6) for Gathering for Women, Shuman HeartHouse and Casa de Noche Buena. The two-year NOFA released October 2025 covers public services, public facilities and infrastructure (CDBG) and homeless services (PLHA).
record.affordability_requirement: CDBG low and moderate income benefit (80% AMI); inclusionary resale units sold to low income first-time buyers; PLHA homeless services for extremely low income households.
record.next_deadline: The FY 2026-27 and FY 2027-28 NOFA (CDBG and PLHA) was released in late October 2025; FY 2026-27 Action Plan adopted and reduced in June 2026 to match program income. Next two-year NOFA expected fall 2027. Rental Assistance Program (General Fund, $250,000 a year) opens monthly application windows.
record.layering_notes: The City of Monterey is its own CDBG entitlement and is not in the Monterey Urban County (county record), but it does not receive HOME directly. Its CDBG money is mostly recycled program income used to buy back, repair and resell inclusionary ownership units rather than to fund new multifamily; multifamily developers should instead look at City-donated land (36-unit MidPen project behind City Hall, Van Buren Senior Housing at 669 Van Buren Street) and the $1.5 million MidPen backup line in the Action Plan. Former RDA housing funds built the Monterey Hotel Apartments and the City owns 8 units at Casa de la Estrella. Water allocation is the binding constraint (Housing Element Program 2-J prioritizes affordable projects for new supply). The NOFA flyer PDF link on the City page returned 404; figures come from the FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan PDF and the 2025 Community Development Department Annual Report, both opened on monterey.gov.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

record.program_name: Inclusionary Housing Program (City Code Section 8-1.00 et seq.), in-lieu fees and inclusionary purchase and resale program
record.administering_agency: City of Monterey Community Development Department, Housing Programs
record.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. The City Code (Section 8-1.00 et seq., Ordinance 3346 C.S. of 2004 requiring permanent affordability) requires a minimum of 20% permanently affordable low and moderate income units in projects of six or more new housing units and in condominium conversions (2015-2023 Housing Element Program i.2.1), with payment of in-lieu fees allowed; the 2015-2023 Housing Element reported that court rulings had limited the ordinance to ownership projects and that it did not apply to apartment projects; the 2023-2031 Housing Element Program 2-I directs the City to codify the requirement in the Zoning Code. The City holds a first right to repurchase deed-restricted ownership units and resells them to low income buyers using CDBG program income ($729,609 generated from such sales in 2025). Portfolio: 531 restricted units (100 inclusionary ownership, 431 deed-restricted rental) plus 42 in development; 2300 Garden Road delivered 13 inclusionary units in a 91-unit project in 2025.
record.affordability_requirement: Low and moderate income units with permanent affordability covenants (2004 ordinance); rental inclusionary units monitored by the Housing Office (about 533 deed-restricted units).
record.next_deadline: Applies at entitlement. Zoning Code codification (Program 2-I) and the density bonus update (Program 2-F, completed by Ordinance 3713 in December 2025) are Housing Element actions due during the 2023-2031 cycle; the Monterey 2031 General Plan update is under way.
record.layering_notes: Section 38-112.5(G)(4) lets on-site inclusionary units also qualify a project for a state density bonus, but payment of in-lieu fees does not. In-lieu fee amounts and the current fund balance were not in the documents opened; the City's municipal code host (municode) blocks scripts, so the ordinance text itself was not read. Program description comes from the FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan and the zoning code cross-reference on the zoneomics mirror. Monterey County's Chapter 18.40 (county record) does not apply inside the city.
record.audit_note: Audit 2026-11-08: redirect was to files.monterey.gov (same PDF). The FY 2026-27 Action Plan confirms the 531-unit portfolio (100 ownership, 431 rental, 42 in development), $729,609 program income from inclusionary unit sales, the first right to purchase, Program 2-I and 2300 Garden Road. It does not state the 20% rule; the City's 2015-2023 Housing Element does, with a six-unit threshold and an ownership-only limit at that time. Whether the City now applies the ordinance to rental projects (post AB 1505) was not confirmed; the code host monterey.municipal.codes returns 403.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

record.program_name: Affordable Housing Density Bonus (City Code Section 38-112.5, Ordinance 3713, December 2025) with local density bonuses, and Regional Housing Needs Assessment Overlay District (Ordinance 3688, 2024)
record.administering_agency: City of Monterey Community Development Department, Planning Division
record.typical_award_size: Incentive, not a subsidy. Section 38-112.5 adopts State Density Bonus Law and adds local bonuses in subsection (J) that are independent of and additional to the state bonus: 10% for consolidating two or more parcels into a lot of at least 0.50 acre; 10% for projects with 70% two- and three-bedroom units (plus one extra story in the Alvarado District and the Pacific, Munras and Cass MF2 overlay); 10% for projects with 40% moderate income units; and 50% for 100% affordable projects under Government Code 65915(b)(1)(G). Rental affordability agreements run 55 years. The RHNA Overlay District (Sections 38-99.9 and 38-99.10) allows multifamily on nonvacant commercial sites carried over from the fourth and fifth cycle inventories, and the Multifamily Residential Overlay sets 60 units per acre.
record.affordability_requirement: State density bonus thresholds; local bonuses require 40% moderate income or 100% affordable (80% AMI and below with up to 20% moderate) as applicable; 55-year covenants for rental units.
record.next_deadline: Not applicable; requested with the first planning application on the City form. Coastal zone projects must also meet the Local Coastal Program except for density.
record.layering_notes: The stackable local bonuses (up to 50% extra for 100% affordable) are the strongest zoning incentive among Monterey County cities and can be combined with the state bonus, inclusionary unit credit and the RHNA overlay sites. No local fee waiver program was found; the City's main constraint is water allocation (Housing Element Program 2-J). Code text read on the zoneomics mirror (Chapter 38, Articles 16E and 17) because the City's municode host blocks scripts.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

record.program_name: Affordable Housing Incentives (Zoning Code Chapter 17.33, density bonus)
record.administering_agency: City of Seaside Community Development Department, Planning Division
record.typical_award_size: Incentive, not a subsidy. Chapter 17.33 grants density bonuses by Council determination on the state sliding scale (10% lower income units earn 20%, rising to 35% at 20%; 5% very low income units earn a 20% bonus on a parallel scale), with incentives and concessions, reduced parking (17.33.050), child care bonuses (17.33.060), processing rules and a recorded density bonus agreement (17.33.100). Bonus units do not count toward the 20% inclusionary requirement. The fifth cycle Housing Element (Program 13) acknowledged the chapter had not been updated to current state law and committed to do so in the comprehensive zoning update.
record.affordability_requirement: State density bonus thresholds; affordability terms per Government Code 65915 (55 years rental).
record.next_deadline: Not applicable; state law controls where the local chapter is less generous. Check for the Seaside 2040 zoning update adoption before relying on local tables.
record.layering_notes: No local fee waiver, trust fund NOFA or city NOFA was found for Seaside beyond the inclusionary in-lieu fund and CDBG (records above and below). Seaside is a CDBG entitlement city (about $365,000 a year per the fifth cycle Housing Element; FY 2026-27 funding plan adopted March 2026 with about $581,000 including carryover, unverified) and is not in the Urban County. Water connection moratorium relief (Council July 2026) matters more than zoning for multifamily feasibility. Code read on the zoneomics mirror because the City site is JavaScript-only for agendas.

record.program_name: CDBG entitlement, Inclusionary Housing In-Lieu Fund and Successor Agency properties (Housing Element funding resources)
record.administering_agency: City of Seaside Community Development Department (Housing and CDBG administration); Successor Agency to the Seaside Redevelopment Agency
record.typical_award_size: FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan (draft, City CDBG page): about $275,000 CDBG entitlement plus $256,750 program income and $49,250 prior year funds, $581,000 total, allocated by Council on March 19, 2026. The FY 2026-28 NOFA anticipated $525,000 (FY 2026-27) and $500,000 (FY 2027-28) and caps planning and administration at 20% and public services at 15%, with the remaining 65% for public facilities and infrastructure; public service grants are guided to $5,000 to $12,000. New housing construction is ineligible except by Community Based Development Organizations, and FY 2026-27 awards went to public services and facility projects (including the Elm House transitional housing roof). The fifth cycle Housing Element (HCD review draft, March 2020) reported an Inclusionary Housing In-Lieu Fund of about $2.6 million as of 2017, historically granted to nonprofit developers to buy existing housing or build new affordable units; no current balance was found. Successor Agency Long Range Property Management Plan sites were identified for residential and mixed use sale.
record.affordability_requirement: CDBG 80% AMI benefit; in-lieu fund projects serve very low, low and moderate income households under Chapter 17.32 covenants.
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. The next two-year CDBG NOFA (FY 2028-30) is expected in late 2027 if the City repeats the prior cycle timing; in-lieu fund awards are ad hoc.
record.layering_notes: Seaside controls three small local layers (CDBG entitlement, in-lieu fund, successor agency land) but CDBG is used for public services and public facilities, not new housing construction, so it is not a gap source for multifamily development. A developer should approach Community Development about the in-lieu fund or sites such as Campus Town (about 297 planned affordable units), the North 40, Parker Flats and 1620 Broadway; the Action Plan also cites the Seaside Housing Collaborative for acquisition and rehabilitation. County HHAP, County Housing Trust Fund and HACM project-based vouchers (county records) are the larger sources. CDBG figures come from the City's CDBG page, the draft FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan and the FY 2026-28 NOFA; the in-lieu fund figure is from the 2020 Housing Element draft hosted by HCD.
record.cycle_notes: CDBG runs on a two-year funding cycle: the FY 2026-28 NOFA was issued November 10, 2025 with a mandatory workshop December 10, 2025 and applications due January 9, 2026; Council approved FY 2026-27 allocations March 19, 2026. In-lieu fund awards are ad hoc by Council action.
eligible_project_detail: public facilities and infrastructure, including nonprofit-owned housing facilities
in-lieu fund grants for acquisition or new affordable construction (ad hoc)
Successor Agency sites for residential sale
record.audit_note: Audit 2026-11-08: the City CDBG page (ci.seaside.ca.us/262) now opens and links the draft FY 2026-27 Action Plan (DocumentCenter View 16790) and the FY 2026-28 NOFA (View 16456). The prior record overstated CDBG at $365,000 a year for acquisition and rehabilitation; current CDBG is public services and facilities. In-lieu fund balance is a 2017 figure.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

record.program_name: Inclusionary Housing (Municipal Code Section 17.48.030 as amended by Ordinance 2025-07) and Affordable Housing Trust Fund (Section 17.48.090)
record.administering_agency: City of Marina Community Development Department, Planning Services Division; City Manager's Office, Housing
record.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Ordinance 2025-07 (introduced May 20, 2025, adopted June 3, 2025, effective 30 days later, implementing Housing Element Program 2.4 with General Plan Amendment Resolution 2025-48) lowered the threshold from 20 to 5 or more units and set a citywide 20% requirement for new or substantially rehabilitated for-sale or rental housing: 6% very low, 7% low, 7% moderate, plus a voluntary incentive-based 10% middle income (up to 135% AMI for-sale) tier; existing occupied housing on the former Fort Ord also 20% (6/7/7), down from 40% (15/15/10). Market-rate density bonus units are exempt. Alternatives approved by Council (17.48.030(D)): land dedication, acquisition and rehabilitation, preservation of at-risk units, conversion of market-rate units, special needs housing, or a tailored program for 500-unit specific plan projects. No in-lieu fee is codified; the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (17.48.090) receives only enforcement recoveries. Rental units restricted 55 years (in perpetuity if allowed), for-sale resale restrictions 45 years, rents capped at 90% of comparable market rent.
record.affordability_requirement: 20% of units: 6% very low (rent at 30% of 50% AMI), 7% low (30% of 60% AMI rental), 7% moderate (30% of 110% AMI rental); middle income tier voluntary.
record.next_deadline: Applies with the first discretionary application (affordable housing plan required). Housing Element objective: 200 lower income units through inclusionary and density bonus by 2031.
record.layering_notes: Marina has no in-lieu fee revenue and therefore no local gap fund; its contribution to affordable deals is land and entitlement through specific plans (The Dunes, Sea Haven, Marina Heights, Cypress Knolls each at 20%) and the Affordable Housing Overlay (record below). Marina is in the Monterey Urban County for CDBG and does not receive PLHA directly (county records). Lightfighter Village received a County Housing Trust Fund loan of $500,115 (county record). Ordinance 2025-07 and Resolution 2025-48 were read as PDFs from cityofmarina.org Archive.aspx; the current code text was read on the zoneomics mirror because marina.municipal.codes returns 403.
eligible_project_detail: market-rate rental and for-sale projects of 5 or more units (compliance)
record.audit_note: Audit 2026-11-08: redirect is to the same ordinance PDF on cityofmarina.org ArchiveCenter. Ordinance 2025-07 confirms the 20 to 5 unit threshold change, the citywide 6/7/7 split with a voluntary 10% middle tier, Fort Ord existing housing reduced from 40% (15/15/10) to 20% (6/7/7) and the density bonus exemption. Minor fix to adoption date; APR reference (93 Dunes BMR units occupied 2024) moved out of next_deadline because its past date was being read as a deadline.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

record.program_name: Affordable Housing Overlay fee waivers and deferrals (Municipal Code Section 17.48.130, Ordinances 2023-01 and 2023-12) and state density bonus adopted by reference (Section 17.48.040, Ordinance 2023-07)
record.administering_agency: City of Marina Community Development Department, Planning Services Division
record.typical_award_size: Projects on Affordable Housing Overlay (AHO) sites mapped for Housing Element opportunity sites receive ministerial administrative approval by the Community Development Director (no hearing), AHO development standards instead of the base zone (42-foot height, 48 feet on Reservation Road and Del Monte Boulevard), and one of three incentives: waived, reduced or deferred planning, plan check or construction permit fees; deferral of City construction and impact fees to completion or occupancy; or payment of construction and impact fees over twelve months or longer after completion. Section 17.48.040 adopts Government Code 65915 to 65918 by reference and caps bonuses, concessions, waivers and parking at the state maximums unless a development agreement provides more. Approvals lapse after two years with a one-year extension.
record.per_unit_cap: Not applicable; fee relief sized to the project's actual City fees.
record.affordability_requirement: AHO projects must meet the overlay's affordability requirements (very low and low income emphasis) and the inclusionary ratios in Table 17.48.030-1; density bonus target units restricted 30 years (55 years when also counted as inclusionary units).
record.next_deadline: Not applicable; ministerial on AHO-mapped sites. Housing Element Program 2.3 committed the City to evaluate its incentives by end of 2024 and strengthen them by end of 2026 if 200 lower income units are not on track.
record.layering_notes: The AHO is the only fee relief program found among Monterey County priority cities and was cited in Marina's August 2025 Prohousing Designation application (Enhancement Category 3). Fee deferral to occupancy helps construction-period cash flow on tax credit deals such as Lightfighter Village (EAH and Veterans Transition Center, 71 units) and future Dunes and Downtown Marina AHO sites. It does not waive school, water (Marina Coast Water District) or Fort Ord Reuse Authority successor fees. Code read on the zoneomics mirror (Title 17, Chapter 17.48) because marina.municipal.codes returns 403.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific rule found. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats fees that are reduced, waived or forgiven by a political subdivision as public funds, but 1720(c)(3) excludes de minimis subsidies (under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost) and 1720 does not address fee deferrals; the outcome depends on the size of the waiver and other project funding. Marina Code Chapter 17.48 (zoneomics mirror) contains no prevailing wage provision.
record.audit_note: Prevailing wage left unclear: only basis is the general Labor Code 1720(b)(4) public-funds definition, with outcome depending on 1720(c)(3) de minimis test and project facts.

record.program_name: Below Market Rate housing program and project affordable housing agreements (Lightfighter Village, The Dunes BMR, Sea Haven BMR; BMR Administrative Policies adopted March 1, 2021)
record.administering_agency: City of Marina City Manager's Office, Housing Program Division
record.typical_award_size: Program, not a cash subsidy. The City records affordable housing agreements under Section 17.48.080 for each project: Lightfighter Village (Veterans Transition Center and EAH Housing, 229-239 Hayes Circle, 71 permanent supportive units, Resolution 2023-34 of April 4, 2023) must keep 40% of units affordable with at least 15% very low income; the agreement restricts 11 units to 30% AMI and 18 units to 50% AMI at TCAC rents for 55 years and the project is securing 17 project-based vouchers. The Dunes BMR site 1 delivered 93 affordable units (occupancy May 1, 2024) and Sea Haven BMR for-sale homes were sold through a 2023 lottery. Housing Element Program 2.5 reserves 30% of BMR units for Marina workers and residents under the BMR Administrative Policies and Procedures (2021).
record.affordability_requirement: Project-specific: Lightfighter 30% and 50% AMI for 55 years; BMR ownership units resale-restricted 45 years; rental inclusionary units 55 years or perpetual.
record.next_deadline: Agreements are approved by Council before building permit on each project. Housing Element objective: assist 60 lower income Marina households through the BMR program and facilitate 200 affordable units by 2031.
record.layering_notes: Marina's role is regulatory and site-based; the money for Lightfighter Village came from County Housing Trust Fund ($500,115), HHAP, state and tax credit sources (county records), and the City contributed entitlements, the AHO process and the 40% affordability agreement. Marina also submitted a draft Prohousing Designation application in August 2025 (draft read on cityofmarina.org) which, if approved, adds state scoring points for Marina sites; designation status not confirmed. The Housing Element APR for 2024 is posted only as a SharePoint link that could not be opened. Documents read: Resolution 2023-34 with the Lightfighter agreement (Archive ADID 13198), Resolution 2025-18 (ADID 14723), the certified Sixth Cycle Housing Element (DocumentCenter View 13793) and the Housing page (cityofmarina.org/190/Housing).
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, successor agency or housing authority. This requirement is imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Spending of in-lieu fee revenue is a separate public funds question. Affordable housing agreements under Section 17.48.080 record restrictions and provide no City funds.

record.program_name: Inclusionary Housing (Municipal Code Chapter 17.41, Ordinance 620 of 2005 as amended by Ordinance 757 of 2023), in-lieu housing fee and Affordable Housing Fund (Section 17.41.080)
record.administering_agency: City of Soledad Community and Economic Development Department; Finance Director administers the Affordable Housing Fund
record.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to residential projects of five or more lots or units and commercial projects of 2,500 square feet or more; the percentage of affordable units is set by the Housing Element (20% is the figure applied to the Miramonte Specific Plan). Compliance by on-site units, land dedication, in-lieu fees or a combination approved by Council; affordable units built concurrently with market-rate units unless an affordable housing developer takes them under an affordable housing agreement (2023 amendment). The in-lieu fee amount and payment method are set by Council case by case (17.41.070) and deposited in the Affordable Housing Fund (17.41.080), which Council may spend only on affordable housing. Exempt: 100% affordable projects, projects of four or fewer units, public and nonprofit service projects. In June 2025 Council voted 3-2 to revise the 132-unit Miravale agreement to replace moderate income units with in-lieu payments and a parcel contribution (press report, about $25,000 a unit proposed), and a Miramonte Affordable Housing Advisory Subcommittee reviewed the ten-phase Miramonte Affordable Housing Plan on May 20, 2026.
record.affordability_requirement: Per Housing Element affordability policies; incentives in 17.41.100 and real property dedication in 17.41.090; eligibility screening and anti-overconcentration rules in 17.41.140 and 17.41.150.
record.next_deadline: Applies at tentative map or permit; obligations due before first certificate of occupancy or final map. Miramonte Affordable Housing Plan expected back to Council in 2026-27; confirm the Miravale in-lieu fee resolution.
record.layering_notes: Soledad's Affordable Housing Fund will be capitalized by Miravale and Miramonte in-lieu payments and could pair with the County PLHA workforce housing set-aside the City requested (record below) for a moderate income for-sale project. Soledad delegated its PLHA to the County in 2024 and is in the state CDBG non-entitlement program, not the Urban County (county records). Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

record.program_name: Density Bonus (Municipal Code Chapter 17.39, Ordinance 753 of October 4, 2023)
record.administering_agency: City of Soledad Community and Economic Development Department, Planning
record.typical_award_size: Incentive, not a subsidy. Chapter 17.39 restates Government Code 65915 to 65918 section by section (state law controls on conflict) for projects with affordable components, child care, senior housing, land donation, 100% affordable, transitional foster youth, disabled veteran or homeless housing and student housing, including the no-minimum-parking rules for lower income rental projects near major transit, senior and special needs projects. No local enhancement beyond state law.
record.affordability_requirement: State density bonus thresholds and 55-year rental covenants.
record.next_deadline: Not applicable; by right with the development application. ADU Ordinance 777 (April 1, 2026) and the Housing Element rezonings are the other recent zoning actions.
record.layering_notes: Soledad has no local trust fund NOFA, fee waiver program or city-run housing NOFA; its tools are the inclusionary Affordable Housing Fund, the County PLHA request and city-owned land (records above and below), plus state non-entitlement CDBG and HOME rounds administered by HCD. Benito Farm Labor Center (HACM) and Senderos transitional housing (14 modular units built with state Encampment Resolution Funds) are the recent affordable projects. Code read on the zoneomics mirror because City hosts were unreachable.

record.program_name: City land for the Soledad homeless youth housing campus (federal Community Project Funding grant B-22-CP-CA-0157, $2 million) and Prohousing Designation pursuit
record.administering_agency: City of Soledad with Monterey County Housing and Community Development Department, Housing Authority of the County of Monterey and CHISPA
record.typical_award_size: The County holds a $2 million HUD Community Project Funding grant (2022, sponsored by Senator Padilla) for a south county housing campus for unhoused parenting youth aged 18 to 24. The City bought a lot next to Vosti Park on Monterey Street with City funds, is demolishing the dilapidated house and remediating the site, and will sell the site to the project using CPF funds; CHISPA will install four to six two-bedroom manufactured homes as permanent supportive housing owned and managed by HACM, with a City, County and HACM services financing plan. Status report to the County 4HS Committee March 26, 2026 (file 26-251). The City's housing web page also states Soledad is pursuing an HCD Prohousing Designation (page not reachable this pass).
record.per_unit_cap: About $333,000 to $500,000 per unit of CPF grant depending on final unit count.
record.affordability_requirement: Permanent supportive housing for transition-age parenting youth experiencing homelessness (extremely low income), consistent with CPF grant terms.
record.next_deadline: Not applicable; single earmarked project. NEPA review and site transfer pending in 2026.
record.layering_notes: Illustrates Soledad's model: city-owned land plus County-held grants (CPF, HHAP youth set-aside in the county HHAP record) and HACM ownership. The County HHAP-6 plan includes $277,969.56 for a permanent supportive housing project with a city partner with a youth set-aside, which likely attaches to this campus. Prohousing Designation would add state scoring points but was not confirmed because cityofsoledad.gov timed out and refused connections on every attempt (fetch helper, WebFetch and curl). Read through the Monterey County Legistar web API and staff report PDF.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal: the HUD FY2022 Community Project Funding Grant Guide v3.0 (https://www.hud.gov/sites/dfiles/CPD/documents/FY22-CPF-Grant-Guide-v.2.0.pdf) states that compliance with Davis-Bacon and Related Acts is not a condition or requirement for CPF grants and applies only if the project also has funds that require it. State: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The CPF grant passes through the County to buy the City site and install manufactured units that HACM will own (report 26-251, https://legistar.granicus.com/Monterey/attachments/446cbf52-6318-4730-8963-e4693920468c.pdf); whether federal pass-through funds are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and whether a housing authority-owned project falls outside the 1720(c)(5) private-project exemptions are project facts (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720).
record.audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: true changed to unclear. Federal Davis-Bacon does not apply to CPF itself.
